title: Universal helmet protection
summary: A comprehensive helmet law paired with sustained enforcement and public communication.
description: The nationwide requirement for riders and passengers on all roads took effect on 15 December 2007. Penalties increased ten-fold, alongside communication and police mobilization.
evidence: A before-and-after study followed patients admitted to 20 hospitals during the first three months after the law.
limitation: Short follow-up, selected hospitals and provinces, no randomized comparison, and simultaneous policy changes limit causal interpretation.
application: Enforce correctly fastened, certified helmets for rider and pillion. Pair enforcement with affordability, quality control and public communication.

title: Automated enforcement
summary: Camera enforcement and transparent reporting can support consistent road-safety delivery.
description: Singapore combines automated and police enforcement with public annual traffic reporting. The cited camera source describes a trial and implementation plans.
evidence: The report describes an operational model, not an isolated estimate of cameras’ causal effect on national fatalities.
limitation: National trends alone do not isolate camera impact. The report notes fatalities rose from 136 in 2023 to 142 in 2024 despite enforcement.
application: Pilot cameras on high-risk corridors; publish speed and casualty outcomes, maintain calibration and provide fair siting, privacy safeguards and due process.

title: Vision Zero
summary: Place human life and physical vulnerability at the centre of system design.
description: Vision Zero expects human error and makes preventing death and serious injury a shared responsibility, with interim targets and sustained delivery.
evidence: The report presents a long-term national framework and governance approach.
limitation: No numerical impact estimate is provided in this report. Long-term national outcomes cannot be promised from a short project.
application: Develop national and state death and serious-injury targets, safer speeds and forgiving roads, backed by funding and accountable agencies.

title: Sustainable Safety
summary: Make road function, design and use work together for safer everyday journeys.
description: A functional road hierarchy and self-explaining infrastructure separate incompatible traffic where practical and protect vulnerable road users.
evidence: The report describes a framework for road design, not a quantified intervention evaluation.
limitation: No numerical impact estimate is provided in this report. Design must fit India’s mixed traffic, informal access and varied road ownership.
application: Classify roads by function and redesign dangerous mixing at high-speed roads, settlement entries, crossings and junctions.

title: Average-speed cameras
summary: Encourage sustained speed compliance across a corridor rather than at one point.
description: Average-speed enforcement assesses compliance across a road section. The cited UK parliamentary answer summarizes a 2016 evaluation.
evidence: An observational evaluation of 50 sites adjusted for regression to the mean and national casualty trends.
limitation: Results are from sites in Great Britain. They are not predicted reductions for India and remain observational evidence.
application: Pilot suitable expressways and high-risk corridors with baseline and control data, transparent siting, lawful data handling and independent evaluation.

title: Staged driver licensing
summary: Build novice drivers’ experience through supervised learning and staged privileges.
description: Victoria’s Graduated Driver Licensing system provides an operational example of supervised learning and limits on higher-risk driving situations.
evidence: The report describes the approach and its potential application; it does not supply a numerical evaluation.
limitation: No numerical impact estimate is provided in this report. Reliable supervision, licensing and enforcement are needed; access barriers must be assessed.
application: Consider staged licensing and risk limits for novice drivers, while protecting access for rural and low-income learners.
